updates.statement: Most of the early wall-time reduction came from cutting the epochs needed to reach 75%, through the backbone and averaging choices: the airbench96 port, Muon, Lookahead and wd ×0.5. With resizing, compile, averaging and backward truncation (stem, whitening, group 2) they give about 11.4x over the organizer's 40-epoch ResNet9 baseline (59.30 s on an A100 80GB PCIe, taken from forks and not run in this loop). That is 5.20 s at the E049 tip (20-seed mean on reused seeds 13–32: 0.7539; seeds 0–2 read 0.7535 and 0.7552 across two builds). No accuracy-per-epoch booster gained ≥0.25 pp after E016. E022, E025, E029, E030, E032 and E044 read null or negative, but most were measured against a baseline just kept on the same seeds (H4.4), so 'flat' fits them as well as 'harmful'. E013/E014 were underpowered. Every keep since E016 cut per-step cost (H2) or spent margin (H4). Large axes are still untested: batch size (H5), plain EMA, LS 0.1, Muon vs SGD (H1.2.2) and hierarchical CIFAR-100 labels (new).
updates.reason: Tip moved to E049 (review: Lvl1 text was stale). Downgraded 'no booster has held up' to 'none ≥0.25 pp detected', because of the post-keep baseline-bias pattern the review documents.

updates.statement: At a fixed epoch count, per-epoch cost is a large lever. Levers found: compile/fusion (−14%, E004); progressive resizing (−22% E007, −2.9% E026, −3.2% E033); and backward truncation on layers that have finished learning. Those are the group-1 freeze over the last 25% (−8.8%, E028, stacked in E034), the whitening detach after 20% (−2.4%, E036) and the group-2 freeze over the last 10% (−4.4% at −0.14 pp, E046; with +0.25 epoch about −2.1% at tied accuracy, E049). Systems overhead is exhausted: GPU idle 2.8% plus non-step kernels 2.5% (E047); CUDA graphs and graph breaks were worth <1% (E015, E017, and Fable). Convs run at 200–270 TF/s, except g1.conv1 at ~0.45x, which is only 6–9% of the step (E047). Limits: truncating a layer that is still learning costs at the dial's rate or worse. Examples: stem freeze from 60% −0.56 pp (E037); intermittent stem backward at 28 px −0.48 pp (E054, implementation unverified); group-2 freeze from 85% −0.24 pp (E053, confounded); stride-2 stem −1.1 pp (E051). Folding BN in the frozen phase saves nothing (E039).
updates.reason: Adds E046/E049/E051/E053/E054 and E047's overhead accounting; tip is now E049.

updates.statement: Removing kernel-launch and Python overhead speeds up each step without changing the math. Compile plus a fused optimizer gave −14% (E004). After that the step is GPU-bound: CUDA graphs gave −0.9% (E015), removing graph breaks −0.5% (E017), and GPU idle is 2.8% (E047). This matches Fable's CIFAR-10 finding that whole-run CUDA graphs were ~0.04 s slower than plain compile. Rebuild variance comes from autotune kernel reselection and is not removed by dropping cudagraphs (E050), so cudagraph mode neither costs nor buys reproducibility.
updates.reason: E050 refuted the idea that dropping cudagraphs fixes rebuild noise; Fable search confirms there is no launch lever.
E044 showed BN recalibration of the averaged weights adds nothing on the tip (paired K=3: −0.003 pp). The calibration mechanism has no support, and the E018 schedule is abandoned.

All 4 committee members expect a refutation. E040 (the same schedule) lost 0.28 pp, and against an unbiased baseline that is probably still ≥0.1 pp. Kept open only because a fresh-seed rerun is cheap; low priority.

updates.statement: Cutting FLOPs per sample through architecture trades time for accuracy at a better rate than cutting epochs. Evidence so far: E010 (576→512 in group 3, ~1.4 s/pp, about the dial); E021 (group-2 width, ~1.0 s/pp, worse); E051 (stride-2 stem conv with the current init, −1.1 pp for −5.6%, ~0.3 s/pp, much worse). E047 shows the convs run efficiently, so MAC cuts translate to time roughly linearly and buy no discount. E051 refutes only that one stem implementation (an init or BN-placement artifact is possible), not stem restructuring generally.
updates.reason: Every architectural cut tested came at or below the dial's rate. Not closed on E051 alone, per review.

3 committee members expect refutation. E047 puts g1.conv2/3 at ~1.9 ms each (~5% of an unfrozen 32 px step, less after the freeze), so the ≥5% saving is unlikely. Group-1 learning still matters late (E037, E054).

updates.statement: Truncating the backward pass saves far more than the truncated FLOP share, but only on layers whose learning has finished. Free cases: the whitening bias after 20% (E036), and group 1 plus whitening over the last 25% (E028, E034: ~23% per frozen 32 px step, nearly half of it memory-bound fused kernels, E043). Group 2 over the last 10% costs about one dial-rate quantity (E046 −0.14 pp for −4.4%; with +0.25 epoch about equal accuracy at −2.1%, E049). Costly cases: stem freeze from 60% (E037 −0.56 pp); conv1-only from 60% (E042 −0.21 pp); intermittent stem backward at 40–70% (E054 −0.48 pp, implementation unverified); group-2 freeze from 85% with an earlier anneal (E053 −0.24 pp, confounded). Folding frozen BN saves nothing (E039).
updates.reason: Adds E049+, E053−, E054−. Reframed around 'learning finished' (review).

updates.statement: If the port trains the whitening bias for the whole run, stopping its gradient after 20% of steps removes the input-gradient of group 1's first conv and the BN/GELU backward feeding it on the 31×31 maps for the remaining steps. (Hiverge actually stops at 0.2 epoch of 7.65, ~2.6% of steps, not 20%; airbench96 stops at 3/45 epochs, 6.7%.) Prediction on the tip: mean time cut by at least 2%, with no more than 0.1 pp loss in the held-out mean.
updates.reason: Corrected the citation per search: Hiverge's detach point is ~2.6%, not 20%. The verdict (E036+) is unchanged. An earlier-detach child has been added.

E046 (−0.14 pp, between thresholds) is not decided. E053's −0.24 pp changed both the anneal start (75→70%) and the freeze start (90→85%), so it is confounded and cannot establish a cliff. Its baseline was E049's draw on reused seeds 13–32.

updates.statement: Decisive test for H2.6.8. On the E036 tip, a group-2 freeze over the last 10% of steps (E046's recipe) combined with a +0.25 true epoch top-up gives a mean time at least 2% below E036. Its 20-seed mean (seeds 13–32) is within 0.03 pp of, or above, E036 run on the same seeds in the same build session. E049 met both clauses nominally (−2.07%; +0.035 pp) but within noise: the SE of the difference is ~0.08 pp, the baseline came from a different build (E044 k0), and E036's own rebuild times span 5.29–5.34 s (−1.7% to −2.6%). Read it as a tie that is ~0.1 s faster, not dominance.
updates.reason: Review: both halves of the rule sit inside noise against a cross-build baseline, and the H4 gate override was never logged. It should not count as closed on a single result within noise.

The committee is split (2 refuted, 2 unknown). E054 says group-1 learning in the 28 px phase is step-limited, which argues for a linear dose and against a pure 32 px-exposure cliff. This is the decisive test between W5's LR-integral and exposure accounts, so it stays open and high priority.

E048 (−0.18 pp for −6.3%, ~1.85 s/pp) and E052 (with a top-up: −0.21 pp vs E049 at −4.1%) both place loss-based selection at or below the dial. The committee unanimously expects refutation, and the notebook closes it.
E048: −0.18 pp against a ≤0.1 pp bound. E052, the stackable form, read −0.21 pp. Two consistent results exceed the bound, though both baselines were on reused seeds.

updates.statement: The binding constraint is the accuracy margin. The tip is E049 (5.20 s): its 20-seed mean on seeds 13–32 is 0.7539, and its seeds 0–2 read 0.7535 and 0.7552 across two builds. Seeds 13–32 have now driven about 9 decisions, so they no longer count as unselected (H4.4), and the population mean is probably ~0.753–0.754. The keep gate has drifted: E027 was kept below its own 0.7535 rule, E033 loosened it to 0.752, E034 fixed 0.7545, and E049 was kept at 0.7539 under a new 'within 0.03 pp' rule with no override logged. The rule that margin comes first (H4.2.6) was skipped. The gate must be derived from P(official 40-seed ≥0.75 on the judge's build) and P(local 3-seed ≥0.753), using measured seed and rebuild noise (new H4 children), then frozen. Locally feasible faster runs (E052 4.99 s, E053 5.07 s; populations ~0.7515) were discarded by a gate never connected to the official bar.
updates.reason: Updated to E049. Records the gate drift and the reuse of seeds 13–32 the review found, and points to a derived gate.

updates.statement: Accuracy noise has four parts. (a) Rebuild noise: a built artifact is deterministic within a build (E050), but every rebuild, with or without cudagraphs, re-draws autotuned kernels. Per-seed shifts are 0.1–0.44 pp, and the seeds 0–2 mean of E036 spread 0.35 pp across four builds (0.7532/0.7525/0.7497/0.7544). How much a rebuild moves a 20-seed mean is unmeasured; if per-seed shifts are correlated it could be 0.1–0.2 pp. (b) Seed and test-set noise: per-seed std is 0.15–0.35 pp. (c) A seed×data-stream component: seed 1 was lowest of seeds 0–2 in 14 of 19 runs from E036 to E054. The deficit vanished in E037, E040, E048, E052 and E054, which change schedule or data order but never the init. So it is a seed×trajectory interaction, not an init property, and no fixed bias correction should be applied. (d) Selection: every seed set used for keeps (3–12, then 13–32) is biased toward the kept tip (H4.4). Changes worth <0.25 pp need 20 fresh seeds per arm plus the rebuild SD.
updates.reason: E050 settles within-build determinism. The seed-1 recount (14/19, and the deficit disappears under data-order changes) weakens the init story, per review. Seed reuse added.
E050: within-build runs are deterministic, but max-autotune-no-cudagraphs builds still differ across fresh processes, so pinning by dropping cudagraphs does not remove the spread.

updates.statement: Seed 1's frequent ~0.3 pp deficit (lowest of seeds 0–2 in 14 of 19 runs, E036–E054) is a seed×data-stream interaction rather than an init property. Offline on the E049 tip: holding seed 1's init fixed and redrawing only the data/augmentation RNG (10 draws) gives a mean ≥0.2 pp above seed 1's usual ~0.751. Redrawing only the init with seed 1's data stream fixed gives a mean ≤0.752. This is diagnostic only and must never be exploited by reordering RNG draws.
updates.reason: Review: E048/E052 change only data order, yet the deficit vanishes. Reversed the predicted direction and lowered confidence in the init explanation.

updates.statement: Near the tip, true epochs are a smooth dial, but its slope is stale. The pre-freeze held-out points (9.5: 0.7577, 9.0: 0.7556, 8.5: 0.7533) gave ~0.44 pp per epoch at ~0.68 s per epoch (~1.5 s/pp). After the freezes, epochs are cheaper and possibly steeper: E046 (−0.14) and E049 (+0.035) imply +0.25 epoch ≈ +0.175 pp (~0.7 pp/epoch), but only across builds. Convention: boosters are ranked by cost per pp, cuts by saving per pp. E045 (+0.20 s for +0.135 pp) is ≈1.5 s/pp, the dial's rate; the notebook's '0.7 s/pp' was an arithmetic error, so its discard reasoning should be redone at the re-measured rate. Only E028/E036's truncations clearly beat the dial; E018, E021, E024, E037, E051 and E054 are clearly worse.
updates.reason: Fixed the E045 arithmetic the review flagged. Added the post-freeze slope hint. Lowered confidence because the dial rate that drives every ranking is unmeasured on the current tip.

updates.statement: Re-measuring the epoch dial on the E049 tip: +0.25 true epoch (~237→~243 steps; resolution, LR, Lookahead, detach and both freezes kept as step fractions) raises the 20-seed mean on fresh seeds 33–52, against E049 on the same seeds, by 0.06–0.18 pp for +0.10–0.16 s, after adding the rebuild SD (H4.5.1) to the comparison SE. This puts the post-freeze dial at ~0.6–2 s/pp and sets the exchange rate for every ranking.
updates.reason: Rebased to the E049 tip and fresh seeds. Widened the upper bound for the steeper post-freeze slope implied by E046/E049. 3 committee members expect support.

updates.statement: Every seed set used to keep a tip becomes biased toward it. The challengers that follow then read ~0.2 pp low on that set: after E017 (E022, E025, E030, E032), after E036 (E040, E041, E042) and after E049 (E052, E053). E038 (seeds 13–22 read 0.19 pp below 3–12 for E036) is the only direct estimate, and seed-set difficulty explains it equally well. Seeds 13–32 have now driven E044–E054 and must be retired as a held-out set. New comparisons use fresh seeds (33–52 onward), with tip and challenger on the same fresh seeds.
updates.reason: Review documents the post-keep pattern across three tips. Raised confidence slightly and extended the claim to seeds 13–32.
3 committee members expect refutation. E040 and E041 each lost ≥0.2 pp individually. Even after a winner's-curse discount, the stacked loss is very likely >0.15 pp.

updates.statement: Muon (Newton-Schulz-orthogonalized Nesterov momentum) on the conv filters, with SGD on BatchNorm biases and the head, reduces epochs-to-75% on CIFAR-100 compared with Nesterov SGD. E006's +0.66 pp confounded Muon, batch 1024→2000 and an RNG re-draw. The only other CIFAR-100 data point (the PR #3 submission, airbench96 128/384/512) reports that Muon lost to SGD at every size.
updates.reason: The search found contrary CIFAR-100 evidence. This raises the value of the clean test H1.2.2.

updates.statement: On the E049 tip, replace Muon on the conv filters with Nesterov SGD (lr and wd scaled for batch 2000, everything else unchanged). Prediction: the 20-seed mean on fresh seeds 33–52 (same seeds for the E049 arm) drops by at least 0.3 pp, and time falls by about 2% (the NS share in E043). If the loss is under 0.15 pp, E006's gain came from batch size or the RNG re-draw; PR #3 predicts this outcome.
updates.reason: Rebased to E049 and fresh seeds. PR #3 is now a concrete counter-prior.

updates.statement: In short CIFAR-100 runs, end-of-run averaging is a first-order lever: Lookahead/EMA gave +0.97 pp at E005, with every seed gaining. No retuning of the airbench Lookahead schedule gained ≥0.15 pp. A harder pull (E025, −0.27 pp), longer free runs (E030, −0.24 pp) and dropping LS late (E032, −0.23 pp) all read negative, but against a baseline just kept on the same seeds (H4.4). So 'local optimum on both sides' and 'LS regularizes the average' are not established; 'flat within ~0.25 pp' fits equally well. With averaging on, the final-LR floor does not matter (E009, C0021). Recomputing BN statistics of the averaged weights adds nothing (E044 paired: −0.003 pp). Untested: plain EMA (H1.3.5); Switch-EMA reports only +0.10 pp on CIFAR-100, so its effect is likely small either way.
updates.reason: Downgraded the local-optimum and LS-mechanism claims per review. Added the Switch-EMA magnitude from search.
Search: Switch-EMA vs plain gives only +0.10 pp on CIFAR-100 ResNet-18, so a ≥0.15 pp change either way is unlikely. Two members expect refutation. Kept open as the one untested averaging variant.
The prediction (≥+0.15 pp) failed regardless of baseline bias, so it stays refuted. The 'hurts' reading in H1.3 is downgraded to 'not helpful' (review).
The prediction (≥+0.15 pp) failed, so it stays refuted. The mechanism 'LS 0.3 regularizes the averaged weights' is withdrawn as unestablished: −0.23 pp against a just-kept baseline is ~2σ at most.

updates.statement: The optimizer and regularization settings copied from CIFAR-10 airbench may not be optimal for short CIFAR-100 runs. The only effect measured on held-out seeds is wd ×0.5 (E016: +0.24 pp, ~2σ); E022's ×0.25 on the SGD groups was −0.24 pp vs E017 but only −0.11 vs E016. LS 0.2/0.3 (E013), Muon lr ×1.5 (E014) and the LR floor (E009) were 'not detected at 3-seed power', not flat. Untested Hiverge/airbench priors (CIFAR-10-tuned, unablated): LS ~0.09, an annealed filter-norm target in place of wd, a frozen BN scale, BN momentum ~0.44, and brightness/contrast jitter.
updates.reason: Added the search's Hiverge/airbench settings as untested priors.
Two members expect refutation. E014's ×1.5 trend was within noise. Unchanged otherwise; low priority.
Two members expect refutation. Hiverge reports no ablation, and part of its record comes from banned TTA (search).

All 4 members expect refutation. With batch-2000 statistics already noisy-enough regularization and wd evidence pointing to over-regularization, ghost BN has a low prior. Kept open but at the bottom of the queue.
Its only test (E029, halved warm-up) read −0.05 pp, flat. The airbench96 auto-research 'faster warm-up' finding did not replicate here.

updates.statement: The airbench96 width allocation is CIFAR-10-tuned, and the 100-way task may be capacity-limited late in the network. However, E047 shows group-3 convs run as efficiently as group 2 (220–270 TF/s), so group-3 capacity is not cheap per MAC. The airbench paper's own airbench96 puts 512 channels in group 2, not in group 3. Reallocating width is therefore expected to trade at about the dial's rate (E010: ~1.4 s/pp), not better.
updates.reason: Review: E047 contradicts the 'cheap small-map capacity' premise, and E021's sublinear scaling is no longer support. Search: the paper's allocation widens the middle.

Re-costed with E047's per-layer table: 512→640 multiplies g3.conv1 by 1.25 and conv2/3 by 1.56, ≈+2.4 ms of conv plus fused BN/GELU per 32 px step ≈ +6–7% time, not ≤2.5%. The prediction's time clause cannot hold, and two members expect refutation.

updates.statement: At a fixed number of data passes, the optimizer step count (batch size) sets accuracy independently of the epoch count. Batch 2000 has not moved since E006, where it was confounded with Muon and an RNG re-draw. Signals point both ways. E045 (more early steps: +0.135 pp, ~1.7σ) and Hiverge's batch 1536 favour smaller batches. The Muon critical-batch theory (b* ∝ (2β+1)(1−β)+λ) says that at this recipe's momentum 0.6 the critical batch is ~6x larger than at β=0.95, which favours larger batches. This is the largest untouched axis.
updates.reason: Added the search's critical-batch theory and the review's point that batch is untested.

3 committee members expect refutation, and the Muon critical-batch theory at β=0.6 disfavours gains from a smaller batch. Kept open because it pairs with H5.1.3/H5.2.1 to separate step-limited from sample-limited learning (review).
Weak theoretical support from the critical-batch formula at momentum 0.6 (search). Still untested.

updates.statement: Accuracy is carried by optimizer steps on layers that are still learning, not by pixels processed. Early on, lowering resolution at a fixed step count is nearly free (E026, E033), while removing steps costs about a uniform trim (E031, E041). E045 (batch 1000 in the 20 px phase) read +0.135 pp for +0.20 s (≈1.5 s/pp, the dial's rate, ~1.7σ). Corollary, narrowed: cutting per-step cost at a fixed step count is cheap only on layers whose learning has finished (stem after 75%, whitening after 20%). It is not cheap in general: E054 (−0.48 pp), E053 (−0.24) and E051 (−1.1) cut per-step cost at a fixed step count and lost.
updates.reason: Review: E054, E053 and E051 contradict the old corollary, so it is restated.

updates.statement: Per-MAC cost is not uniform across layers, but the non-uniformity is memory-bound elementwise traffic on large activations, not tensor-core inefficiency. E043: fused BN/GELU/pointwise kernels are 27% of a 32 px step. E047: every conv except g1.conv1 runs at 200–270 TF/s, and g1.conv1 (0.45x) is only 6–9% of the step. Freezing a block also skips its BN/GELU backward and optimizer traffic, which is why the freezes beat their FLOP share (E028, E046: the committee counterexamples). Remaining identical-math levers are small: cheaper activations (H6.5.1, doubted by all members), BN statistics on a subset (new), and Cin padding (H6.4.2, ≤~1.5%).
updates.reason: Folded in E047. H6.1 and H6.4 refuted. The E028/E046 counterexamples are explained by H6.6.
E047 shows 7×7 and 3×3 convs at full efficiency, so E021's sublinear MAC scaling is not explained by tile size. Only E024's 26 px result remains as support.

E043: non-GEMM kernels are ~31% of the 32 px full step (≥30% met). The stem freeze saved 7.7 of 33.5 ms, about half in fused kernels. The '≥35% for group 1 + whitening' clause was not measured directly, but it is consistent with that saving plus the forward cost.

E047: g1.conv1 does run at ~0.45x group-2 efficiency, but it is only 2–3 ms (6–9%) of a 33.5 ms step, because dgrad is skipped after the detach. It is not the main part of what E028/E036 saved, which was dgrad/wgrad and fused kernels on the 31×31 maps (E043).
E047: conv1 is at 0.45x group-2 TF/s (the first clause holds) but takes only 6–9% of step GPU time, below the 10% bar.

updates.statement: Math-identical padding: widen the whitening conv's output from 24 to 32 channels with 8 zero filters (zero, detached bias) and zero input channels in group-1 conv1. This keeps every output identical while aligning Cin to tensor-core tiles. It cuts mean time on the E049 tip by at least 1% (conv1 forward + wgrad is ~2 ms per unfrozen step at 0.45x efficiency, E047). Accuracy stays within rebuild noise.
updates.reason: Lowered the threshold from 2% to 1% to match E047's measured ceiling (~1–1.5% overall). Rebased to E049.

The ReLU route is doubted by all 4 members (Inductor may already recompute GELU in the fused backward, per W5's crux). The search adds BN-statistics sampling and a Welford/two-pass check as the remaining routes into the 27% share; children added.
All 4 members expect refutation. If Inductor recomputes GELU from the BN output inside the fused backward, ReLU saves <2% of bytes. Hiverge chose SiLU, not ReLU, and published no ablation.

updates.statement: Backward truncation in any group saves about 1.5–2x that group's backward FLOP share, because a frozen block also skips its BN/GELU backward (memory-bound), its Muon/SGD update and its Lookahead traffic. This explains the committee counterexamples E028 (27% of a 32 px step saved against a ~12% FLOP share) and E046 (~10 ms per frozen group-2 step, beating every forecast). It also explains E031's time miss: per-step cost is almost entirely pixel- and step-proportional (E047: idle + non-step ≈5%), so removing steps saves time in proportion. Per-group freeze value should be estimated from profiled time, not MACs.
updates.reason: All 4 members vote supported. It is the mechanism for three counterexamples, but the direct profile (H6.6.1) is still unrun, so it stays open.

new.statement: The binding resource is optimizer steps on layers that are still learning. Time can be saved without accuracy cost only where a layer's learning has finished: the whitening bias after ~5–20%, the stem after ~75%, and group 2 not before ~90%. Steps that still update a learning layer are worth about the dial's rate wherever they sit (E037, E041, E045, E053, E054). Measuring per-group learning progress therefore predicts which freeze, detach and batch changes are free, and blind dose sweeps become unnecessary.

A layer's remaining contribution is tracked by its relative update rate (||ΔW||/||W|| per window of steps, or the gradient norm relative to its peak). Freezing a group costs ≤0.1 pp of population accuracy once that rate has fallen below a fixed fraction of its peak, and costs at about the dial's rate before that point.

One instrumented offline run of the E049 tip (seeds 33–35, real data, outside submissions/arena/) logs per-group ||ΔW||/||W|| per 5 steps for whitening bias, group 1, group 2, group 3 and head. Prediction: the curves order the known outcomes correctly. The whitening bias drops below 10% of its peak rate by ≤10% of steps; group 1 only after ~70% (consistent with E037 and E054 costing and E028 being free); group 2 only after ~88% (consistent with E053 costing and E046 being marginal). If the curves fail to separate E028 from E037, the learning-finished account is refuted as a predictor.

Rebuild noise is correlated across seeds. A rebuild therefore moves a 20-seed mean by a build component (SD ~0.08–0.2 pp), not just by per-seed noise averaged away. Every keep decision since E044 used thresholds of 0.03–0.15 pp and is under-powered unless this SD is added to the comparison SE.

Build E049 (commit 3df6233) twice in fresh processes with private inductor caches and run each build on the same fresh seeds 33–52. Prediction: the two 20-seed means differ by ≥0.08 pp, and the per-seed differences correlate positively across seeds (the mean shift exceeds per-seed SD/√20). If they differ by <0.04 pp, the 20-seed mean is build-robust and the E044–E054 decisions stand at their stated power.

The keep gate should be derived from two probabilities and then frozen: P(official 40-seed mean ≥0.75 on the judge's own PCIe build) and P(local 3-seed mean ≥0.753). Inputs are the fresh-seed population mean, the 40-seed SE (~0.05 pp), the rebuild SD (N2.1) and a judge-build drift term. Under such a gate, candidates with population ~0.7515 (E052, E053) pass the official bar with high probability, so the current 0.7545 gate over-prices margin.

Run E052 (ce17ae7) and E053 (f30d362) on fresh seeds 33–52 alongside E049. Prediction: both population means are ≥0.751, and with the measured rebuild SD the computed P(official ≥0.75) is ≥0.9 for each. Their deficit vs E049 on the fresh seeds is ≤0.15 pp, smaller than the −0.21/−0.24 measured on E049's reused seeds 13–32.

Winner's curse on seeds 13–32: E049, kept on seeds 13–32 at 0.7539, reads at least 0.1 pp lower on fresh seeds 33–52 in the same build. If it reads within 0.05 pp, the post-keep ~0.2 pp challenger deficits are real effects, not baseline bias.

E054's −0.48 pp is partly an implementation artifact. In an offline unit test of the alternating stem step on synthetic data, at least one of the following fails: (a) group-1 params, grads and Muon momentum buffers are bit-unchanged across a detached step; (b) the next full step's update equals a reference that never ran the detached variant; (c) BN running stats and Lookahead state behave identically. If all three pass, E054 stands as evidence that stem learning in the 28 px phase is step-limited.

The whitening bias finishes learning far earlier than 20% of steps (Hiverge detaches at ~2.6%, airbench96 at 6.7%). On the E049 tip, moving the whitening detach (with its LR annealed to 0) from 20% to 6% of steps cuts mean time by 0.3–0.7% and loses no more than 0.05 pp on fresh seeds 33–52 against E049 on the same seeds. The time effect is below the rebuild time spread (~1%), so judge time on per-step CUDA-event timing, not wall time alone.

BatchNorm statistics from a subset: on the E049 tip, compute training-BN mean/var over 1/4 of each batch (a strided slice inside the compiled graph; normalization still applied to the whole batch) in group 1 and group 2 only. This cuts mean time by ≥2% and loses ≤0.1 pp on fresh seeds 33–52. Only the forward reduction gets cheaper, so the saving is bounded by the BN-stat share of the fused 27%.

In the E049 32 px step, at least one training-BN reduction on the 31×31 or 15×15 maps compiles to a two-pass or split reduction under channels_last (visible in the Inductor output and as a kernel achieving <60% of HBM bandwidth in the E043-style trace). If none does, the fused BN share is already near its bandwidth floor and the identical-math route into H6.5 closes.

CIFAR-100's 20 coarse superclass labels, which ship with the training set, can supply extra training signal at zero per-step cost: smoothing mass placed on same-superclass classes, or an auxiliary coarse-label loss. This raises fine-label accuracy per epoch in short runs, a structural sample-efficiency gain of the kind H1 says scalar sweeps cannot reach. Precondition: RULES.md and the data loader must allow coarse labels as part of the 50k training data.

If the rules allow coarse labels: on the E049 tip, hierarchical label smoothing (LS total 0.3, with half of the smoothing mass spread over the 4 same-superclass fine classes and half uniform) raises the 20-seed mean on fresh seeds 33–52 by ≥0.15 pp against E049 on the same seeds, at unchanged time.

Fidelity check by code read: airbench96(_faster) and Hiverge both freeze the BatchNorm scale (weight.requires_grad=False). If the port trains it, freezing it on the E049 tip changes the 20-seed fresh-seed mean by no more than ±0.1 pp and cuts time by ≥0.5% (fewer SGD params, less fused backward). If the port already freezes it, close this by reading the code.

structured_output.summary:
I rebased the tree onto the E049 tip (5.20 s; 20-seed mean 0.7539, measured on seeds that have been reused for many decisions) and applied the review's corrections.

**Verdicts settled**
- **H2.7 / H2.7.1 refuted.** Loss-based sample selection came in at or below the epoch dial's rate twice (E048, E052).
- **H4.1.5 refuted (E050).** Dropping CUDA graphs does not remove the build-to-build accuracy spread.
- **H6.4 / H6.4.1 refuted (E047).** g1.conv1 runs at about 0.45x group-2 efficiency, but it is only 6–9% of the step.
- **H6.3.1 supported (E043).** Non-GEMM kernels take about 31% of the 32 px step.
- **H2.3.3 and H1.7.1 retired.** E044 showed BN recalibration adds nothing. Re-costing H1.7.1 with E047's per-layer table gives about +7% time, against its ≤2.5% claim.

**Downgraded because the evidence is within noise**
- **H2.6.9 → inconclusive (E049).** E049 met both rules only nominally: +0.035 pp with an SE of 0.08, against a baseline from a different build. Its −2.07% time is inside E036's rebuild time spread.
- **H2.6.8: E053 is confounded.** It moved both the anneal start and the freeze start, so it cannot show a cliff.
- **H2.5 → inconclusive.** E051 refutes only the stride-2 stem with the current init.
- **H1.3 and H1:** "local optimum" and "no booster held up" become "nothing ≥0.25 pp detected". Most of those negatives were measured against a baseline that had just been kept on the same seeds.

**Restated mechanisms**
- **H4:** E049 was kept without a logged gate override. The gate has drifted from 0.7535 to 0.752, 0.7545 and then "within 0.03". Seeds 13–32 are no longer unselected.
- **H4.1:** Seed 1 was lowest in 14 of 19 runs. Its deficit disappears when only the data order changes, so it is a seed × data-stream effect, not an init effect. H4.1.6's predicted direction is reversed to match.
- **H4.2:** Fixed the E045 arithmetic: it is about 1.5 s/pp, not 0.7. The dial's slope after the freezes is stale and possibly steeper. H4.2.6 is rebased to fresh seeds.
- **H5.2:** Narrowed to "cutting per-step cost is cheap only on layers that have finished learning". E051, E053 and E054 contradict the general version.
- **H6:** Rewritten around memory-bound elementwise traffic. The E028, E046 and E031 time counterexamples are explained through H6.6 (confidence raised to 0.6).
- **H6.5.1 (ReLU), H1.5.9 (ghost BN), H4.4.1 and H2.3.8:** lowered, since all or most committee members expect them to be refuted.
- **H1.2 / H1.2.2:** H1.2 lowered and H1.2.2 rebased to the E049 tip and fresh seeds 33–52. The CIFAR-100 PR #3 reports that Muon lost to SGD, which makes H1.2.2 the decisive test.
- **H5:** Now holds the Muon critical-batch argument from the search: at momentum 0.6 it predicts a larger critical batch.
- **H2.6.3:** Citation corrected: Hiverge detaches the whitening bias at about 2.6% of steps, not 20%.

**New hypotheses**
- **N1 (new Lvl1):** time is saved without accuracy cost only on layers that have finished learning. Its test, N1.1.1, is a single instrumented run tracking per-group relative weight change, to pick freeze points.
- **N2 / N2.1:** measure how much a rebuild moves a 20-seed mean (two fresh builds of E049 on seeds 33–52).
- **N3 / N3.1:** derive the keep gate from the probability of passing the official 40-seed bar, and re-score E052 and E053 on fresh seeds.
- **N4:** a winner's-curse test of E049 on seeds 33–52.
- **N5:** a unit test of E054's alternating step before that branch is closed.
- **N6:** detach the whitening bias earlier (about 6% of steps).
- **N7, N8:** BN statistics computed on a subset of each batch, and a check for two-pass BN reductions in the compiled step.
- **N9 / N9.1:** use CIFAR-100's coarse superclass labels as extra training signal (needs a RULES.md check first).
- **N10:** check by reading the code whether the port trains the BN scale, which airbench and Hiverge both freeze.

**Lvl1 status:** H1, H2 and H4 are supported. H5, H6 and N1 are open.
